messages.content: Kansas City got a small wrinkle. The Sunday Delta connection moved later, so I land closer to 6:55 pm instead of 6:20. The hotel also emailed that early check-in is unlikely because they are sold out Saturday. Badge pickup is Sunday evening at the institute hotel, and I will have my carry-on plus the recruitment materials shipment to deal with.
What time does badge pickup close, and did the hotel confirm they can hold your shipped materials and luggage at the desk? That decides whether we route hotel-first or venue-first.
Badge pickup is 7:30 to 8:30. The hotel can hold packages; they just will not promise a room before standard check-in. Monday badge pickup reopens at 7:30, but first session is 8:30.

Go hotel first as the base plan. With a 6:55 landing, assume curbside around 7:20, hotel around 7:50, drop the carry-on and confirm the materials are held, then reach badge pickup around 8:05 if the hotels are close. The early check-in warning mostly means no midday room; still mark the reservation as late arrival.
If the app says landing 7:10 while I am in the connection airport, do I still try for Sunday badge pickup?

Yes, if pickup is open until 8:30 and the ride estimate is under 30 minutes. If wheels-down slips after 7:20 or the terminal is messy, skip Sunday pickup and use Monday. I would not drag the carry-on or materials through the venue for a maybe.
Airport to hotel is rideshare, right? I have not used the new MCI setup.

Rideshare is fine for MCI. Use the designated app pickup at the terminal and keep the taxi stand as backup if surge looks silly. A rental on Sunday adds garage, return, and parking friction for very little value.
What about Tuesday dinner in the rain? The restaurant is about 15 minutes south. I hate the idea of getting stranded, but a rental feels excessive.

Stay with rideshare for Tuesday too. Call it 20 minutes early, and ask the restaurant to help call a cab back if storms slow the apps. A short rental is only worth it if the forecast turns into severe-weather alerts or you add multiple errands. For Wednesday, check out before the partner breakfast, leave bags with the hotel, and order the airport ride by 2:15 for the 4:45 flight.

messages.content: I have the first draft of an August recruitment loop and need to make it coherent before I ask the office to approve it. Monday afternoon high-school visit in Fort Collins, Tuesday counselor breakfast in Boulder, Tuesday evening fair in Denver, Wednesday morning visit in Colorado Springs, and Thursday noon transfer-center meeting in Pueblo. Starting from Salt Lake City. Can you compare drive versus fly and rent versus one-way routing?

Yes. Before I rank them, what are the exact event times, how much recruitment material are you moving, and are you free to leave Sunday afternoon or only Monday morning? Those affect the arrival buffer a lot.

Fort Collins is 2:15 to 3:00 Monday. Boulder breakfast 7:30 to 8:30 Tuesday. Denver fair 6:00 to 8:30 Tuesday. Colorado Springs visit 9:30 Wednesday. Pueblo meeting noon to 1:00 Thursday. I will have a carry-on and one 25-pound rolling display bag. I can leave Sunday afternoon if needed, but I would rather not lose the whole Sunday.

Quick comparison: fly into Denver and rent is the cleanest if you can keep Monday unhurried; driving your own car is simplest for materials but costs you a long SLC-to-Colorado day on each end; a one-way plan only helps if you finish near Colorado Springs and can avoid the drive back to Denver. For reliability, I would not use a Monday flight that lands after about 10:30. That still gives rental pickup, the drive north, lunch, and a cushion before Fort Collins.
I would rather avoid a dawn flight, but I do not want the Fort Collins visit to start with me already tense.

Then the two practical versions are Sunday late-afternoon flight into Denver, or a Monday morning flight that lands by 10:30. Sunday costs one more hotel night but makes Monday calm. Monday saves the night, but a delay, rental line, or traffic north can eat the whole buffer. A noon Denver arrival is too tight for a 2:15 Fort Collins visit.
The office might approve Sunday night if it prevents a same-day-arrival problem. What would the Sunday-in, Thursday-home timeline look like?

Sunday: fly SLC to Denver late afternoon or early evening, pick up the rental, sleep Fort Collins or Loveland. Monday: do the Fort Collins visit, then drive to Boulder or a nearby U.S. 36 area hotel. Tuesday: Boulder breakfast, work/admin block, then Denver Tech Center area for the evening fair. Wednesday: drive to Colorado Springs for the morning visit, then decide whether to sleep Colorado Springs or Pueblo. Thursday: Pueblo at noon, then either COS for a later afternoon flight or DEN for an evening flight.
The Denver fair is at a school near the Tech Center. I do not need downtown. I do need an easy dinner after the fair.

That points to DTC, Greenwood Village, or maybe Lone Tree for Tuesday night. You should get easier parking than downtown, lots of chain-hotel options, and restaurants still open after an 8:30 fair. I would not pay downtown rates for this loop.
Where should Monday night be: Boulder proper, Longmont, or just stay in Fort Collins?

Fort Collins is too far for a 7:30 Boulder breakfast. Longmont is workable if you want easier parking and rates, but it adds a morning drive. Boulder proper is the calmest if the breakfast is central or on campus, though it may cost more. Louisville or Superior can be a middle ground if Boulder rates are high.
The Boulder breakfast is near Pearl Street. Longmont sounds a little risky for that early.

For Pearl Street at 7:30, I would lean Boulder if the rate is acceptable. If Boulder is overpriced, use Louisville or Superior rather than Longmont; you stay on the right side of the commute and still avoid some Boulder parking pain. Since breakfast is part of the event, hotel breakfast that morning matters less.
Do I need to ship materials, or can I fly with them?

If the display bag is checked-size, I would avoid making it the only copy of your materials. Put essentials in your carry-on: visit folder, name tags, QR sheet, and a small brochure stack. Ship a non-critical box to the first hotel or Fort Collins host, and include a return label if you can.
It is the rolling display bag, technically checked size. I can ship a small box to the first hotel.

Then fly-and-rent still works. Ask the Sunday hotel to accept packages under your name and arrival date, and confirm any handling fee. Keep Monday-critical items with you. If the office wants the full fair kit every day, driving becomes more attractive, but for one shipped box plus carry-on essentials, flying is fine.
What is the clean hotel sequence for the approval note?

Sunday: Fort Collins or Loveland. Monday: Boulder, or Louisville/Superior if Boulder is too expensive. Tuesday: DTC or Greenwood Village. Wednesday: Colorado Springs north if you want better dinner choices and a short drive after the school visit; Pueblo if you want the easiest Thursday morning. With a noon Pueblo meeting, Colorado Springs still works.
If we finish Pueblo around 1:00, which airport routing should I ask them to price?

Ask for two priced versions. Primary: fly SLC to DEN Sunday late afternoon or early evening, rent at DEN, return the car at DEN Thursday, and fly home after 6:30 pm. Secondary: same inbound, but drop the car at COS and fly home after about 4:00 pm if the fare plus one-way rental fee is not much higher. Driving is the backup if materials get heavier. In the approval note, flag package acceptance at the Sunday hotel, parking costs in Boulder and DTC, and meals: event breakfast Tuesday, easy DTC dinner Tuesday, and a simple Wednesday dinner in Colorado Springs or Pueblo.

messages.content: The Front Range loop changed before I booked anything. Colorado Springs moved to Wednesday afternoon, and they added a short Thursday morning counselor coffee near downtown Denver. Pueblo is now unrealistic. Rental car prices are lower than expected, but downtown Denver hotel parking is ugly, and the Boulder hotels with the easiest breakfast have stricter cancellation dates. Help me clean this up.

Got it. Is Pueblo fully dropped rather than postponed, and what time is the Thursday coffee? The answer changes whether we should still consider Colorado Springs airport or keep everything tied to Denver.
Pueblo is dropped for this round. Thursday coffee is 8:30 to 9:15 near Union Station. I would like to be home Thursday afternoon, not late evening.

That makes the ranking clearer. First choice: fly into and out of DEN with a round-trip rental. Second: drive your own car if the office wants the lowest simple cash cost or if materials grow. Third: one-way or COS return, now not useful, because Thursday pulls you back to Denver anyway. I would avoid downtown hotel nights unless the rate includes parking, which is unlikely.
Would you still fly in Sunday night, or is Monday morning okay now?

Monday morning is okay if the flight lands at DEN by 10:30 and you are not waiting on a checked display bag. Fort Collins at 2:15 still needs a cushion for rental pickup and the drive north. Sunday is calmer, but with Pueblo gone and rental prices lower, Monday morning is a defensible approval request.
I will ship materials to the first hotel and carry the visit folder with me. Let's plan on Monday morning if there is a flight that lands before 10:30.

Then use this sequence: Monday fly SLC to DEN, pick up the rental, Fort Collins visit, then sleep Boulder or Louisville/Superior. Tuesday Boulder breakfast, then the Denver Tech Center fair, and sleep DTC or Greenwood Village. Wednesday keep that Denver-area hotel for a second night, drive to Colorado Springs for the afternoon visit, and come back after.
Same Denver hotel Tuesday and Wednesday? I was wondering if moving after Colorado Springs would be smarter.

Stay put Tuesday and Wednesday. Moving after the Colorado Springs visit creates a late check-in and another parking question. DTC or Greenwood Village keeps Tuesday easy and usually has restaurants nearby. For Thursday, leave around 7:30 for Union Station, pay for one downtown garage, then head to DEN after the coffee.
How should I handle the Boulder cancellation issue versus breakfast?

Prioritize cancellation while the hosts are still shifting things. Since Tuesday breakfast is the counselor event, an included hotel breakfast Monday night is nice but not worth a strict cancellation penalty. If Boulder proper has a reasonable cancellable rate, take it. If not, Louisville or Superior with easy parking is the safer approval choice.
What exactly should I send for sign-off?

Send this: Monday morning SLC-DEN flight landing before 10:30, round-trip rental from DEN, materials shipped to the first hotel, Fort Collins visit at 2:15, Monday night in Boulder or Louisville/Superior on a cancellable rate. Tuesday: Boulder counselor breakfast, then DTC fair, with Tuesday and Wednesday nights at one DTC/Greenwood Village hotel that has reasonable parking and nearby dinner. Wednesday: drive to Colorado Springs for the afternoon visit and return to Denver after. Thursday: Union Station coffee 8:30 to 9:15, return the rental at DEN, and fly home after about 12:30 or 1:00. Note the downtown hotel was avoided because parking would erase the convenience.
